fields.limitations: The previously reviewed pipeline described first-in-human initiation as the next step. Its latest wording cannot be reverified because that endpoint remains HTTP 403 and verification-pending; the registry, CTIS and Zealand's dated 13 August 2026 interim report corroborate initiation. ClinicalTrials.gov estimates completion on 6 September 2027; CTIS lists an estimated EU trial end of 30 June 2027. These separately scoped estimates are retained without reconciliation. This dose-escalation study assesses safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics; recruitment is not proof of efficacy or safety. Co-formulation is a development aim, and preclinical combination and antiemetic findings are not human combination benefits.

fields.summary: 710GO is an investigational oral peptide acting at melanocortin-3 and melanocortin-4 receptors. ANZCTR ACTRN12626000541303 (710GO-HV-01 Parts A/B), updated 2 July 2026, lists a randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled Australian Phase 1 study as recruiting, with actual first enrolment on 21 April 2026, a target of 120 and 11 enrolled at that update. The separately registered Part C food-effect crossover study ACTRN12626000540314, last updated 30 April 2026, still lists not yet recruiting and a target of 12.
fields.limitations: The 28 May 2026 sponsor announcement reported first dosing and approximately 100 planned participants. Its count is retained separately from the later dose-escalation registry's 120 target; 11 is a dated accrual count, not current enrolment or a result. Part C's recruitment start remains anticipated, not actual. Both records give anticipated last enrolment on 2 November and last data collection on 31 December 2026, with no study results posted. Differences in population wording, counts and recruitment timing remain unresolved. ClinicalTrials.gov discovery remains incomplete; these ANZCTR records provide official alternatives. Neither first enrolment nor dosing establishes human efficacy or safety. Weight, fat, lean-mass, tolerability, maintenance and combination observations in the earlier announcement concern preclinical studies, not human benefits, strength, function, durability, superiority or an approved regimen. The separate mifomelatide cancer-cachexia programme is not obesity evidence.
